qs.q: During beta-oxidation of a saturated fatty acid with an odd number of carbons, the final cleavage yields propionyl-CoA. What vitamin cofactor is required to convert propionyl-CoA into succinyl-CoA?
qs.e: Methylmalonyl-CoA mutase requires a coenzyme B12 derivative to rearrange methylmalonyl-CoA into succinyl-CoA.

qs.q: During beta-oxidation of odd-chain fatty acids, propionyl-CoA is produced as a final product. How is this intermediate successfully funneled into the tricarboxylic acid cycle?
o: It is directly converted into acetyl-CoA by oxidative decarboxylation
It is reduced to propanol and excreted safely through the kidneys
It condenses with oxaloacetate to form a seven-carbon tricarboxylic acid
It enters the urea cycle as a substitute for ornithine and citrulline
It is carboxylated to succinyl-CoA via a biotin-dependent pathway
qs.e: Propionyl-CoA is carboxylated to D-methylmalonyl-CoA, isomerized to L-form, and then rearranged into succinyl-CoA to enter the TCA cycle.
